attack_summary: Non-count pattern; primary attack was IMPOSED-vs-REAL. The core reveal (10:22 you->them iltifat) is REAL and classically named, verified verbatim in al-Jalalayn. Breaks are confined to peripheral framing (cross-passage 'repeats', secondary attributions, a superlative), which are fixable and do not touch the load-bearing spine.

substrate_check.10:22: 2MP open (yusayyiru+KUM 2MP obj; kuntum 2MP) -> 3rd person block (jarayna 3FP ships; bihim 3MP; farihu 3MP; ja'at-ha 3FS; ja'a-humu 3MP; zannu 3MP; uhiTa 3MS PASS; bihim 3MP; da'aw 3MP) -> quoted vow anjay-TA-na (najja 2MS + 1P) addressed to God. CONFIRMED in corpus features.
substrate_check.6:63: tad'una 2MP (call upon Him, 3MS obj) then quoted vow anja-NA = 3MS verb + 1P ('if HE saves us'). NOT 2nd-person address to God. Proposal correctly does not claim otherwise. CONFIRMED.
substrate_check.6:64: second-pass finding: dry-land ingratitude is 2nd person — thumma ANTUM tushrikuna (antum 2MP + tushrikuna 2MP). So 6:63-64's forgetting is addressed as 'you', NOT distanced to 'them'. Directly contradicts the 'forgets Him into He/them on dry land' half of the headline. CONFIRMED.
substrate_check.10:23_dryland: second-pass finding: within the PRIMARY passage the ghayba does not persist onto land — yabghuna 3MP is immediately followed by a return to 2nd-person address (ya ayyuha al-nas; baghyu-KUM 2MP; anfusi-KUM; marji'u-KUM; nunabbi'u-KUM). So even in 10:22-23 'dry land = them' is only the narration verb, not the sustained register. CONFIRMED.
substrate_check.17:67: addressee stays 2MP throughout (massa+kum, tad'una 2MP, najja+kum, a'radtum 2MP); God referenced 3MS (iyyahu). No khitab->ghayba turn. CONFIRMED.
substrate_check.31:32: entirely 3rd person (ghashiya-hum, da'aw 3MP, najja-hum, min-hum). No 2nd-person address at all. CONFIRMED.
substrate_check.disguised_count: NO. Person/tense/voice are fixed morphological features, not a frequency tally.

broken_claims: THESIS WORDING (false as stated): 'the same choreography repeats across the other sea-rescues (6:63, 17:67, 31:32).' The you->them->You arc occurs ONLY in 10:22. 17:67 keeps 2nd-person throughout (no ghayba turn); 31:32 is wholly 3rd-person (no khitab at all); 6:63 quotes the vow in 3rd person ('if HE saves us'), not 2nd; and 6:64 addresses the dry-land ingratitude in 2nd person (antum tushrikuna), not 'them'. The choreography does NOT repeat — the verses VARY. Must reword.

ATTRIBUTION CREEP (risks section): 'the you->them->You turn WITHIN 10:22 is classical iltifat (al-Zamakhshari, al-Jalalayn, named).' Only the you->them (khitab->ghayba) turn at wa-jarayna bihim is classically catalogued. The snap-back to 'You' (anjaytana, 2MS+1P) is quoted passenger supplication — the article's own structural observation, NOT a second catalogued iltifat. Do not attribute the snap-back to the mufassirun.

UNVERIFIED NAMED SOURCES: al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) and al-Razi citations unverified with available tooling; Zaynab's own cardinal sin is naming unverified classical attributions. Only al-Jalalayn is confirmed.

OVERCLAIM (why_now): 'the single most citable example in the classical balagha tradition.' 1:5 (iyyaka na'budu, ghayba->khitab) is the more canonical stock example; 10:22 is A well-known example, not THE single most citable. Cosmetic, soften.
required_corrections: 1) Reword the thesis so 6:63/17:67/31:32 are presented as VARIATIONS on the sea-rescue address (17:67 keeps 'you' throughout; 31:32 stays 'them' throughout; 6:63 quotes the vow in the third person), NOT as a repeated identical choreography — only 10:22 dramatizes the full you->them->You arc; keep the honestly-flagged 'modern structural reading' label on the four-verse synthesis. 2) Restrict the classical iltifat attribution to the you->them turn at wa-jarayna bihim (al-Jalalayn, verified verbatim); frame the return to 'You' (anjaytana) as the passengers' quoted supplication and the article's own reading, not a mufassir-named iltifat. 3) Independently verify the al-Kashshaf and al-Razi citations against primary text before naming them, or drop them and lead solely with the verified al-Jalalayn attribution. 4) Soften 'the single most citable example in the classical balagha tradition.'
